title: Prompt Miniaturization Sketches
content:
Purpose: quick brain-dump for shrinking prompt surface area while keeping downstream quality. Goal is to produce templates and few-shot sets that are 'token-frugal' for streaming/edge usage and cheaper hosted calls.

Notes / principles:
- Minimize redundancy across instruction + exemplars. If an instruction can be implied by exemplar pattern, drop repeated phrasing.
- Use tightly-formatted slot labels (e.g., Q:, A:, S:) to reduce ambiguity without long sentences.
- Prefer 2–3 concise exemplars over 5 verbose ones if they cover the distribution.
- Put high-signal features (labels, key phrases) early in the prompt to benefit KV caching and prefix reuse.

Experiments to run (short-term):
1) Baseline: full verbose prompt (control). Metrics: ROUGE/F1 for summary tasks, accuracy for classification, token cost, latency.
2) Compact template v1: remove polite scaffolding, keep 3 short exemplars.
3) Compact exemplars (suffix compression): move instruction hints into 1-line header and compress each exemplar to 1 sentence.
4) Hybrid: compressed instruction + 1 exemplar + dynamic suffix instruct (generated by model).
Measure: quality delta per 100 tokens saved.

Compact templates (working drafts):
- Compact template v1 (classification):
IN: <TEXT>
TASK: label emotion (joy/sad/angry/neutral)
EX1: "Movie makes me cry" => sad
EX2: "So pumped for this" => joy
EX3: "This is fine" => neutral
OUT:
- Compressed-instruction chat style (for streaming):
System: "You are a concise classifier. Reply only with one label."
User: "Text: <TEXT>\nLabel:"
- Minimal-slot template (for generative rewrite):
SRC: <text>
OUT: rewrite (<=30 tokens):

Few-shot set (micro exemplars) — extractive highlight task:
Example 1:
SRC: "The delivery arrived late and the packaging was damaged."
HL: "delivery arrived late"
Example 2:
SRC: "Product excellent but instructions unclear"
HL: "instructions unclear"
Example 3:
SRC: "Great customer service, will buy again"
HL: "Great customer service"

Prompt assembled (minimal):
TOOL: ExtractImportant
SRC: <SRC>
EXS:
1| delivery arrived late
2| instructions unclear
3| Great customer service
OUTPUT: top highlight

Observed failure modes (notes):
- Token truncation: long exemplars chopped off leading to ambiguous labels. Mitigation: use token counters, prefer shorter exemplars or append exemplars as external context when possible.
- Overfitting to exemplar wording: model repeats phrasing too literally. Try label-only exemplars (example -> label) to teach abstraction.
- Degenerate outputs when instruction too terse (model hallucinates additional instructions). Fix: single-line constraint "Reply with one token: <label>" as a guardrail.
- Tokenization edge-cases: emojis and punctuation increase token counts unpredictably; test with sample distribution.

Concrete micro-experiments (A/B):
- A: 3 verbose exemplars, instruct full sentence. B: 3 single-line mapping exemplars (X => y). Evaluate top-1 accuracy and calibration.
- A: instruction at top. B: instruction repeated in each exemplar. See impact on prefix caching across batch.
- Temperature sweep for compressed prompts: are compressed prompts more temperature-sensitive? test temp 0.0, 0.2, 0.6.

Small example run (for summarization budget):
Task: compress user feedback to <=12 tokens + sentiment tag
Compact prompt idea:
HEADER: "Compress to <=12 tokens | tag: positive/neutral/negative"
EX1: "Had to wait 2 weeks, packaging torn." => "waited 2w, torn pkg | negative"
EX2: "Loved the colors, fit perfect." => "great fit, color | positive"
IN: "Item shows up late and missing screws"
OUT:
Expected: "late arrival, missing screws | negative"

Design questions / open hypotheses:
- Does exemplar diversity beat exemplar concision for tail cases? My guess: concision wins for head distribution; diversity helps rare phrasing. Need to stratify by frequency bins.
- Can a tiny model distill exemplar patterns into a short instruction that generalizes better? Try few-shot distillation: ask larger model to produce a single-sentence instruction that captures exemplars, then use that as compact instruction.
- How does prefix KV reuse behave when we move instruction to system role vs inline? Instrument latency and cache hit rate.

Implementation checklist (next steps):
- [ ] Create small dataset (2k samples) stratified by freq and length.
- [ ] Run tokenized length analysis and build histogram.
- [ ] Implement prompt variants in prod playground (hosted API) and log token counts + outputs.
- [ ] Create eval harness for guardrail violations (label-only responses, extra text).

Quick heuristics for teams:
- If unit cost is >$0.0005/token for your workload, prioritize exemplar compression.
- For streaming SLOs, keep system + header <120 tokens to maximize prefix reuse and reduce cold-start latency.
- Use label-only outputs when downstream parsing is fragile; otherwise prefer short natural language for human-readability.

Random notes to self (scattered):
- Try "slot-collapse": convert multi-part exemplars into numbered compact rows. See if model uses pattern.
- Check impact of punctuation removal from exemplars. Might reduce tokens but hurt clarity.
- Evaluate micro-examples with partially masked exemplar (remove one word) and see if model recovers pattern -> measures generalization.

End of sketch. Keep iteration light. Save distilled templates to repo /prompt-mini and link to eval pass once >80% of full-prompt baseline with <=30% token usage.
